claims.text: ABM reframed mastitis as a spectrum of conditions resulting from ductal inflammation and stromal edema
claims.quote: scientific evidence now demonstrates that mastitis encompasses a spectrum of conditions resulting from ductal inflammation and stromal edema

claims.text: Inflammatory mastitis can come before bacterial mastitis
claims.quote: If ductal narrowing and alveolar congestion are worsened by overstimulation of milk production, then inflammatory mastitis can develop, and acute bacterial mastitis may follow

claims.text: Antibiotics for inflammatory mastitis disrupt the microbiome and increase risk of progression to bacterial mastitis; reserve antibiotics for bacterial mastitis
claims.quote: Use of antibiotics for inflammatory mastitis disrupts the breast microbiome and increases the risk of progression to bacterial mastitis.

claims.text: ABM states antibiotics should be reserved for bacterial mastitis
claims.quote: Reserve antibiotics for bacterial mastitis.

claims.text: Mastitis contributes to early weaning; bacterial mastitis can progress to phlegmon or abscess
claims.quote: contributes to early cessation of breastfeeding

claims.text: Progression to phlegmon or abscess
claims.quote: This can progress to phlegmon or abscess, particularly in the setting of tissue trauma from aggressive breast massage.

claims.text: Engorgement: bilateral pain, firmness, swelling usually days 3 to 5 postpartum
claims.quote: It presents as bilateral breast pain, firmness, and swelling that usually occurs between days 3 and 5 postpartum.

claims.text: Engorgement is related to interstitial edema and hyperemia during secretory activation (lactogenesis II)
claims.quote: postpartum engorgement that results from secretory activation (lactogenesis II) is a distinct clinical entity related to interstitial edema and hyperemia

claims.text: Engorgement recommendations: hand expression, reverse pressure softening, lymphatic drainage, ice
claims.quote: Perform reverse pressure softening of the areola

claims.text: Engorgement recommendations include lymphatic drainage and ice
claims.quote: Consider lymphatic drainage to alleviate interstitial edema

claims.text: Ductal narrowing results from alveolar distension and/or mammary dysbiosis
claims.quote: related to alveolar distension and/or mammary dysbiosis

claims.text: Repeated feeding to clear a plug suppresses FIL, increases milk production, worsens inflammation and narrowing
claims.quote: will suppress FIL, increase milk production, and ultimately exacerbate inflammation and ductal narrowing

claims.text: Squeezing or aggressive massage to push a plug out is ineffective and causes tissue trauma
claims.quote: by squeezing or aggressively massaging the breast are ineffective and result in tissue trauma

claims.text: Physiologic breastfeeding is the right approach for ductal narrowing
claims.quote: physiological breastfeeding and antiinflammatory measures as described hereunder are most efficacious

claims.text: Inflammatory mastitis can cause fever, chills, tachycardia without infection
claims.quote: systemic signs and symptoms such as fever, chills, and tachycardia. It should be emphasized that systemic inflammatory response syndrome may occur in the absence of infection.

claims.text: Swedish study: most women with inflammatory mastitis resolved without antibiotics
claims.quote: A Swedish study noted that most women with inflammatory mastitis had complete resolution of symptoms without need for antibiotics or other interventions.

claims.text: Reassure patients that many symptoms resolve with conservative care and psychosocial support
claims.quote: Reassure mothers that many mastitis symptoms will resolve with conservative care and psychosocial support.

claims.text: Bacterial mastitis presents as cellulitis in one region that may spread to other quadrants
claims.quote: Bacterial mastitis presents as cellulitis (worsening erythema and induration) in a specific region of the breast that may spread to different quadrants

claims.text: Common organisms: Staphylococcus (S. aureus, S. epidermidis) and Streptococcus species
claims.quote: Common organisms in lactational mastitis include Staphylococcus (e.g., S. aureus, S. epidermidis, S. lugdunensis, and S. hominis) and Streptococcus

claims.text: Bacterial mastitis needs antibiotics or probiotics to resolve
claims.quote: a progression from ductal narrowing and inflammatory mastitis to an entity necessitating antibiotics or probiotics to resolve

claims.text: Phlegmon: firm mass-like area without fluctuance after worsening mastitis
claims.quote: Phlegmon should be suspected with a history of mastitis that worsens into a firm, mass-like area without fluctuance

claims.text: Deep massage may promote phlegmon
claims.quote: Excessive deep tissue massage in the setting of ductal narrowing and inflammatory mastitis may propagate phlegmon formation

claims.text: Phlegmon is a heterogeneous, ill-defined collection
claims.quote: Phlegmons are heterogeneous, complex, and ill-defined fluid collections

claims.text: Phlegmon may need extended antibiotics, case by case
claims.quote: Lactational phlegmon may require extended antibiotics for complete resolution, but cases should be considered individually.

claims.text: Phlegmon can coalesce into a drainable abscess; follow closely
claims.quote: A phlegmon may coalesce into a drainable abscess and, therefore, patients should be followed carefully

claims.text: Abscess develops in approximately 3 to 11% of women with acute mastitis
claims.quote: Approximately 3–11% of women with acute mastitis will develop an abscess.

claims.text: Abscess is an infected fluid collection needing drainage for source control
claims.quote: progression from bacterial mastitis or phlegmon to an infected fluid collection that necessitates drainage

claims.text: Drain the abscess for source control
claims.quote: Drain the abscess to achieve source control.

claims.text: Needle aspiration often first-line but most patients need repeat aspirations
claims.quote: Needle aspiration with fluid culture and sensitivity is often recommended as the first-line intervention for lactational abscess. However, patients most often require recurrent aspirations for definitive resolution.

claims.text: Repeat aspirations are stressful and risk breastfeeding discontinuation
claims.quote: Repeated aspirations may be stressful and discouraging for the patient, and risk breastfeeding discontinuation.

claims.text: Consider drain placement at the first procedure, office or interventional radiology
claims.quote: Drain placement as the initial intervention should be considered for definitive management at the time of the index procedure.

claims.text: Interventional radiology referral for drain placement
claims.quote: Patients also can be referred to interventional radiology for drain placement.

claims.text: Drains to gravity not suction; avoid vacuum-assisted wound devices
claims.quote: Drains or skin stents should be placed to gravity rather than suction

claims.text: Strictly avoid vacuum-assisted wound devices on a lactating breast
claims.quote: Strictly avoid vacuum-assisted wound devices on a lactating breast.

claims.text: Continue breastfeeding from the affected breast after aspiration or drain placement
claims.quote: After aspiration or drain placement, mothers should continue breastfeeding from the affected breast.

claims.text: Milk fistula in fewer than 2%, with lactation managed and hyperlactation treated
claims.quote: Milk fistula rate is <2%, but lactation must be managed appropriately and hyperlactation treated if present.

claims.text: Antibiotics commonly 10 to 14 days after drainage; shorter if cellulitis resolves quickly
claims.quote: Antibiotic duration is commonly 10–14 days; however, a shorter course may be appropriate if there is rapid resolution of surrounding cellulitis.

claims.text: Inflammation can take weeks to settle; follow-up exam and imaging
claims.quote: Tissue inflammation and phlegmonous changes may take several weeks to resolve

claims.text: Follow-up exams and imaging to confirm resolution
claims.quote: They should undergo interval examination and imaging to ensure resolution.

claims.text: Abscess: progressive firmness/redness, palpable collection in a well-defined area
claims.quote: Abscess presents as a progressive induration and erythema, and often a palpable fluid collection in a well-defined area of the breast

claims.text: Fever may settle, settle and return, or worsen until drained
claims.quote: fever may resolve as the body walls off the infectious process, or may resolve and then recur

claims.text: Subacute mastitis: needle-like burning pain, blebs, recurrent induration
claims.quote: Patients may have needle-like, burning breast pain, nipple blebs, recurrent areas of induration or congestion

claims.text: Subacute mastitis reflects chronic dysbiosis with biofilms narrowing ducts
claims.quote: Subacute mastitis occurs when ductal lumens become narrowed by bacterial biofilms in the setting of chronic mammary dysbiosis.

claims.text: Subacute mastitis has milder local symptoms, usually no systemic symptoms
claims.quote: systemic symptoms are uncommon and local breast symptoms are milder than in acute mastitis

claims.text: Recurrent mastitis has no consensus definition; symptoms every 2 to 4 weeks or less often
claims.quote: There is no consensus on the definition of recurrent mastitis. Patients may describe having mastitis symptoms such as fever, breast redness, breast swelling, and/or breast pain that occur every 2–4 weeks, or less often.

claims.text: Recurrent mastitis risk factors: hyperlactation, dysbiosis, inadequate prior treatment, unaddressed cause
claims.quote: Risk factors include waxing and waning episodes of hyperlactation, dysbiosis, inadequate treatment of prior mastitis, and failure to address the underlying etiology of prior episodes.

claims.text: Milk stasis postulated but causation not proven
claims.quote: Milk stasis has been postulated to be a potential instigating factor for mastitis, although scientific evidence has not proven a causation.

claims.text: Hyperlactation is a primary underlying risk factor
claims.quote: Attention should be given to appropriate treatment of hyperlactation as an primary underlying risk factor for mastitis.

claims.text: Hyperlactation feeds a cycle of congestion, inflammation and dysbiosis
claims.quote: Hyperlactation predisposes patients to luminal congestion and inflammation, which in turn facilitates mammary dysbiosis.

claims.text: Dysbiosis is a disruption of the milk microbiome; factors include antibiotics, pumps, Cesarean births
claims.quote: Mammary dysbiosis, or disruption of the milk microbiome, results from a complex interplay of factors, including maternal genetics and medical conditions, exposure to antibiotics, use of probiotics, regular use of breast pumps, and Cesarean births.

claims.text: Increased milk removal increases production
claims.quote: Milk volume depends on a feedback mechanism whereby increased milk removal increases production.

claims.text: Pumping to empty perpetuates hyperlactation and worsens edema and inflammation
claims.quote: perpetuates a cycle of hyperlactation and is a major risk factor for worsening tissue edema and inflammation

claims.text: Express only the volume the infant takes
claims.quote: Mothers using breast pumps should express only the volume their infant consumes.

claims.text: Pumping may predispose to dysbiosis
claims.quote: and may, therefore, predispose to dysbiosis

claims.text: Deep massage causes inflammation, edema and microvascular injury
claims.quote: Deep massage causes increased inflammation, tissue edema, and microvascular injury.

claims.text: Light sweeping of the skin (lymphatic drainage) is preferred over deep massage
claims.quote: with light sweeping of the skin rather than deep tissue massage

claims.text: Nipple trauma associated with mastitis but data limited by confounding and bias
claims.quote: Although nipple trauma is associated with mastitis, the data are limited by confounding and bias.

claims.text: Mastitis not caused by retrograde spread of bacteria from visible nipple trauma
claims.quote: mastitis is not caused by retrograde spread of pathogenic bacteria from visible nipple trauma

claims.text: Cesarean birth associated with delayed lactogenesis II
claims.quote: Cesarean birth is associated with delayed lactogenesis II

claims.text: Specific foods do not cause mastitis
claims.quote: No evidence exists that specific foods cause mastitis

claims.text: No scientific evidence for candida mastitis
claims.quote: no scientific evidence exists to support this diagnosis

claims.text: Poor hygiene not a cause; routine sterilization not needed; handwashing and basic pump cleaning
claims.quote: There is no evidence to support poor hygiene as a cause of bacterial mastitis or the need for routine sterilization of pumps. Handwashing before milk expression and basic pump cleaning practices should be followed.

claims.text: Clean pump parts after each use; routine sterilization of pumps and household items unnecessary
claims.quote: Pump parts should be cleaned appropriately after each use, but routine sterilization of pumps and other household items

claims.text: Mastitis often presents in a segmental area
claims.quote: Mastitis is inflammation of the mammary gland that most often presents in a segmental distribution of ducts, alveoli, and surrounding connective tissue

claims.text: Consider milk culture if no improvement after 48 hours of first-line antibiotics (MRSA)
claims.quote: If there is no symptomatic improvement after 48 hours of first-line therapy, consider a milk culture to evaluate for resistant and/or less common pathogens such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

claims.text: Early culture for NICU expressed milk, health care workers in high-MRSA areas, recurrent infections
claims.quote: Other situations in which to consider early milk culture include mothers expressing breast milk for an immunocompromised infant in the neonatal intensive care unit, health care workers in areas with a high prevalence of MRSA, and patients with recurrent infections.

claims.text: Culture can be done for subacute mastitis
claims.quote: Sterile milk culture and sensitivities can be performed

claims.text: MRSA and resistant CoNS do not respond to dicloxacillin or cephalexin
claims.quote: MRSA and resistant CoNS will not respond to typical antibiotics used for acute mastitis such as dicloxacillin or cephalexin.

claims.text: Bacterial mastitis not contagious, no risk to infant, no interruption of breastfeeding
claims.quote: Bacterial mastitis is not a contagious entity and does not pose a risk to the infant nor require an interruption in breastfeeding.

claims.text: Safe for children to consume milk from a breast with bacterial mastitis
claims.quote: It is safe for children to consume milk from a breast with bacterial mastitis.

claims.text: If no milk can be removed due to swelling, pause feeds from affected breast in acute phase
claims.quote: the mother should not continue to attempt feeding from the affected breast during the acute phase

claims.text: Feed from the other breast and return as swelling settles
claims.quote: She can feed from the contralateral breast and return to feeding from the affected breast when edema and inflammation subsides.

claims.text: Hand-express small volumes for comfort
claims.quote: Mothers can hand express small volumes of milk for comfort

claims.text: Feed first from the less congested breast to avoid overstimulation
claims.quote: feeding first off the left, less congested breast first to avoid overstimulation of the affected right breast

claims.text: Ice and NSAIDs reduce edema and inflammation
claims.quote: Ice and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) can reduce edema and inflammation

claims.text: Ibuprofen 800 mg every 8 hours; acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 8 hours in the acute setting
claims.quote: Ibuprofen can be dosed 800 mg every 8 hours and acetaminophen/paracetamol 1,000 mg every 8 hours in the acute setting.

claims.text: Ice can be applied every hour or more often
claims.quote: ice can be applied every hour or more frequently if desired

claims.text: Sunflower or soy lecithin 5 to 10 g daily by mouth to reduce ductal inflammation and emulsify milk
claims.quote: Sunflower or soy lecithin 5–10 g daily by mouth may be taken to reduce inflammation in ducts and emulsify milk.

claims.text: Avoid deep massage
claims.quote: Avoid deep massage of the lactating breast.

claims.text: Avoid vibrating devices
claims.quote: Avoid electric toothbrushes and other commercial vibrating or massaging devices.

claims.text: Avoid saline soaks, castor oil and other topical products
claims.quote: Avoid saline soaks, castor oil, and other topical products.

claims.text: Cabbage leaves no more effective than ice
claims.quote: Studies have not demonstrated cabbage leaves to be more effective than ice

claims.text: Cabbage may carry Listeria
claims.quote: Importantly, cabbage may carry Listeria bacteria.

claims.text: Do not unroof nipple blebs
claims.quote: do not unroof the bleb as this will cause trauma and further luminal narrowing

claims.text: Prophylactic antibiotics not shown to prevent mastitis and may select resistant strains
claims.quote: Prophylactic antibiotics have not been shown to be effective in the prevention of mastitis and may select antibiotic-resistant strains.

claims.text: Systemic symptoms lasting more than 24 hours point to bacterial mastitis / need evaluation
claims.quote: An evaluation by a medical professional should be performed if there are persistent systemic symptoms (>24 hours) such as fever and tachycardia.

claims.text: No response to conservative measures suggests bacterial mastitis
claims.quote: diagnosis should be considered if the breast is not responding to conservative measures

claims.text: First-line dicloxacillin or flucloxacillin 500 mg QID for 10 to 14 days
claims.quote: Dicloxacillin or flucloxacillin 500 mg QID for 10–14 days

claims.text: First-line cephalexin 500 mg QID for 10 to 14 days
claims.quote: Cephalexin 500 mg QID for 10–14 days

claims.text: Cephalexin: broader coverage incl. gram-negative rods; no need to separate from meals
claims.quote: Broader coverage including gram negative rods; does not need to be taken separately from meals

claims.text: Second-line clindamycin 300 mg four times daily for 10 to 14 days
claims.quote: Clindamycin 300 mg four times daily for 10–14 days

claims.text: Second-line TMP-SMX DS twice daily for 10 to 14 days
claims.quote: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS BID for 10–14 days

claims.text: TMP-SMX not recommended with infant G6PD deficiency; caution with premature or hyperbilirubinemic infants, especially under 30 days
claims.quote: Not recommended for mothers of children with G6PD deficiency. Use with caution in mothers with premature infants or infants with hyperbilirubinemia, especially under 30 days old.

claims.text: First-line options have a low relative infant dose
claims.quote: All drugs have low Relative Infant Dose of the drug.

claims.text: Women should not be told to express and discard milk
claims.quote: Women should not be instructed to express and discard their milk, as bacterial mastitis is not a contraindication to breastfeeding.

claims.text: Recurrent: examine and culture to confirm true recurrent mastitis rather than treat empirically
claims.quote: Examine patients and obtain milk culture to establish a diagnosis of true recurrent mastitis, rather than treating empirically.

claims.text: CoNS common in milk but can be opportunistic pathogens
claims.quote: although CoNS are commonly present in breast milk, they have also been identified as opportunistic pathogens in mastitis.

claims.text: Review breastfeeding and pumping in recurrent mastitis
claims.quote: Evaluate breastfeeding and/or pumping for potential risk factors for mastitis

claims.text: Pumps can injure the breast with wrong flange, high suction, long sessions
claims.quote: Breast pumps also can cause trauma to breast parenchyma and the nipple areolar complex if improper flange sizes are used, suction is too high, or the mother is pumping for an excessive duration of time.

claims.text: ABM advises avoiding nipple shields; inadequate extraction
claims.quote: shields represent nonphysiological breastfeeding and result in inadequate breast milk extraction

claims.text: Avoid nipple shields
claims.quote: Available evidence does not support the use of nipple shields.

claims.text: Probiotic data mixed; strong recommendation could not be made
claims.quote: A systematic review suggested that probiotics may be effective for both treatment and prevention of mastitis, but a strong recommendation could not be made due to limitations of the studied trials.

claims.text: Probiotics should contain L. fermentum or, preferably, L. salivarius strains
claims.quote: the probiotic should contain Limosilactobacillus fermentum (formerly classified as Lactobacillus fermentum) or, preferably, Ligilactobacillus salivarius (formerly classified as Lactobacillus salivarius) strains

claims.text: Consider daily probiotics for prevention of recurrent mastitis
claims.quote: Consider daily probiotic use with L. fermentum or, preferably, L. salivarius for prevention

claims.text: Only selected strains may be effective; results cannot be generalized to a species
claims.quote: Note that only selected strains of these bacterial species may be effective against mastitis pathogens. Therefore, clinical trial outcomes cannot be generalized to an entire species

claims.text: Multiple recurrences in the same location warrant radiology evaluation (mass, granulomatous mastitis)
claims.quote: Multiple recurrences in the same location warrants radiology evaluation to rule out an underlying mass or other abnormality such as granulomatous mastitis.

claims.text: Any concern for IBC warrants urgent referral to breast surgery and oncology
claims.quote: Any concern for inflammatory breast cancer warrants urgent referral to breast surgery and oncology.

claims.text: Erythema may present less conspicuously on darker skin
claims.quote: keeping in mind that erythema may present less conspicuously on darker skin.

claims.text: Ultrasound and same-day radiology/breast surgery consult when abscess, phlegmon or infected galactocele suspected
claims.quote: When an abscess, phlegmon, or infected galactocele is suspected, ultrasonography and prompt (same-day) consult with radiology and breast surgery are recommended.

claims.text: Focal discrete swelling/redness or symptoms beyond 24 to 48 hours raise concern for phlegmon/abscess
claims.quote: If symptoms are ongoing or progressing for more than 24 to 48 hours and are coupled with a focal, discrete area of swelling and erythema, the clinician should consider a phlegmon, abscess, or infected galactocele.

claims.text: Lymphatic drainage: light sweeping toward axillary and supraclavicular nodes

claims.quote: Second-line treatment is clindamycin 300 mg 4 times daily or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160 mg/800 mg twice daily, each for 10 to 14 days.

claims.text: Milk culture if symptoms persist after 48 hours of antibiotics to rule out MRSA
claims.quote: If symptoms persist after 48 hours of antibiotic treatment, obtain a breast milk culture from the affected breast to rule out methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and other resistant pathogens.

claims.text: Refer to breast specialist to rule out IBC when symptoms do not respond to antibiotics
claims.quote: Referral to a breast specialist is advisable to rule out inflammatory breast cancer in patients whose symptoms do not respond to antibiotics.

claims.text: Lactation consultant or breastfeeding medicine specialist can help downregulate supply
claims.quote: Consider referral to a lactation consultant or breastfeeding medicine specialist who can help downregulate supply safely if the patient has an oversupply or hyperlactation.
